overall_assessment: No personal data leaks in the 28 sampled courses: staff lists (HTML 'Fagperson(er)', old PDF 'Fagpersoner/Fagpersonar' with '-Name (Role)'), OpenURL resolver links and their user_ip are removed completely, and reference authors are kept. The main defect is the 2020-2025 PDF version stamp ('CODE_1 Bokmål Versjon 31.Mai.2026'), left in 1512 of 2728 plans; the academic-year slash regex and the season-year regex also strip some reading-list content. One leak outside the sample: in 3 MGL2042-1 plans (2020-2021) the course coordinator's name is left on an inline 'Studiepoeng 15 Emneansvarlig <name>' line, because .role_name_line_regex needs the role label at the start of the line.

findings.description: Every 2020-2025 PDF-layout plan keeps the document version stamp 'CODE_1 Bokmål|Nynorsk Versjon DD.Month.YYYY' as its second line. Only the trailing HH:MM was removed. This is an administrative revision date, which the rubric says must be removed. All 20 suspects have it; the 8 random controls (2014-2019 HTML and old-PDF layouts) do not. Institution-wide: 1512 of 2728 plans, every year 2020-2025. normalize_plan_text() strips only the year, so 'versjon 31.mai.' stays in the dedup text: 12 more distinct plans (1299 vs 1287) than with the stamp removed. The line above it, 'Dette er studietilbudet for studieår .', is a harmless dangling label.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: .anon_uis() strips the version header only in its pre-2020 PDF form '^\s*EMNE\s+\S+\s+\S+\s+Versjon' (uppercase EMNE prefix, e.g. 'EMNE MGL2121_1 NYNORSK Versjon 19.Jun.2020 09:23') and the HTML form 'Emnebeskrivelsen er hentet fra ...'. The current PDF header has no 'EMNE' prefix. The generic dd.mm.yyyy pattern does not match a month name ('31.Mai.2026'), and the generic time pattern removes only '21:50'.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_uis(), make the EMNE prefix optional, or add str_remove_all("(?m)^[ \\t]*\\S+_\\d+[ \\t]+(?:Bokmål|Nynorsk|Engelsk|English)[ \\t]+Versjon[^\\n]*(?:\\n|$)"). At the same time, drop the emptied '^Dette er studiet(?:ilbudet|ilbodet) for studieår\\s*\\.?\\s*$' line. Add a test in tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R ('MGL3066_1 Bokmål Versjon 31.Mai.2026 21:50\nTittel' -> 'Tittel'), rerun tar_make() and explain the metrics_check change (about 1500 uis plans).

findings.description: The academic-year pattern removes any 'dddd/dd(dd)'. In reading lists it cuts the date path out of URLs ('psykologisk.no/2014/11/...' -> 'psykologisk.no//...', 'idunn.no/npt/2012/03/...' -> 'idunn.no/npt//...'). It also damages DOIs ('10.1007/978-3-030-...' -> '10.-3-030-...') and deletes publication-year pairs such as '(1980/2005)' or '2004/2012', which the rubric says to keep. Institution-wide, outside the OpenURL links already stripped, it removes 392 URL path segments in 190 plans, 8 DOIs and 17 reprint-year pairs in 13 plans, but only 13 real academic years in 11 plans. At uis it does more harm than good.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_generic(): str_remove_all("\\b\\d{4}/\\d{2,4}\\b") runs unconditionally. Unlike the dash form, it has no consecutive-year check (.drop_academic_year) and no URL guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the slash rule with str_replace_all("(?<![/.\\w])\\d{4}\\s?/\\s?\\d{2,4}\\b(?!/)", .drop_academic_year), widening the pattern in .drop_academic_year() to [-–/]. Only consecutive years outside URL paths and DOIs are then removed. Add test cases for 'https://psykologisk.no/2014/11/x', 'doi:10.1007/978-3-030-1', '(1980/2005)' (kept) and 'studieåret 2023/2024' (removed).

findings.evidence: Utdanningsdirektoratets spørreundersøkelse til lærere [−høsten 2020−] Karl Solbue Vika
findings.description: The generic season-year rule removes 'høsten 2020' from the title of the NIFU report 'Spørsmål til Skole-Norge høsten 2020: Analyser og resultater fra Utdanningsdirektoratets spørreundersøkelse til lærere'. That is a literature reference title, which must be kept. It affects all 4 sampled MGLT43-1 offerings; institution-wide about 27 reading lists contain a season-year, though some, like 'Retorikk-pensum NOR165 høsten 2021', are semester labels that may go. The same mechanism explains the pre-pass 'artifact' flag on MGL2050-1/MGL1050-1 2021, though that part of the plan is truncated in the packet. There, the time rule turns a video's duration 'juli-terroren [20:28]' into '[]', and the dd.mm.yyyy rule removes the video's publication date ('Martine Rauken, 19.10.2021,' -> 'Martine Rauken, ,').
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_generic(): the season-year, dd.mm.yyyy and HH:MM rules run over the whole plan, including the 'Litteratur' reading list, where dates and times belong to the references.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_generic() (or .anon_uis()), split the text at the first '(?m)^Litteratur\\s*$' heading. Apply only the personal-data rules (e-mail, staff lines, OpenURL, user_ip, phone) to the reading-list tail, not the season-year, date, academic-year and time rules. Add a test that 'Spørsmål til Skole-Norge høsten 2020' and '[20:28]' are kept under 'Litteratur'.
